## About VisioForge — Video & Audio SDKs for .NET & Delphi
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/about

# About Us

VisioForge is a small software company based in Bilbao, Spain. Since 2008 we have been building video and audio SDKs that developers around the world use to add capture, playback, editing and streaming to their own applications.

## Our History

VisioForge was founded in 2008. The first products were Windows SDKs built on DirectShow. That classic engine still powers Video Capture SDK .NET, Media Player SDK .NET and Video Edit SDK .NET on Windows, together with the Delphi and ActiveX components of the All-in-One Media Framework.

As .NET moved beyond Windows, we built a second, cross-platform engine on top of GStreamer. The X engines — VideoCaptureCoreX, MediaPlayerCoreX and VideoEditCoreX — and the pipeline-based Media Blocks SDK .NET run the same C# code on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.

In 2025 and 2026, releases added a complete ONVIF implementation for IP cameras, .NET 10 support, Uno Platform and Unity integration, an MCP server that gives AI coding assistants direct access to the SDK documentation, on-device AI blocks for object detection, face recognition, OCR and speech-to-text, an ASP.NET Web Forms HLS player, and native Windows on Arm support.

## Our Mission

Our mission is to empower developers by providing high-quality, reliable, and easy-to-use multimedia SDKs. We are committed to innovation, exceptional customer support, and delivering solutions that meet the evolving needs of the software development community.

## What We Offer

-   •**.NET SDKs**: Video Capture SDK .NET, Media Player SDK .NET, Video Edit SDK .NET and Media Blocks SDK .NET cover recording, playback, editing and custom media pipelines on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android. Video Edit SDK FFmpeg .NET adds FFmpeg-based editing on Windows, and Video Fingerprinting SDK, for .NET and C++, finds duplicate and pirated video.
-   •**DirectShow filters for C++, Delphi and .NET**: The FFmpeg Source and VLC Source filters, the Encoding Filters Pack and the Processing Filters Pack plug into any DirectShow application on Windows. Video Encryption SDK protects video and audio files with AES-256, and Virtual Camera SDK adds a virtual webcam and microphone that Zoom, OBS and browsers see as real devices.
-   •**Delphi and ActiveX SDKs**: The All-in-One Media Framework brings video capture, playback and editing to Delphi (RAD Studio) as native VCL components, and to VB6, C++ Builder and other COM-compatible environments as ActiveX controls.

## Cross-Platform Support

Video Capture SDK .NET, Media Player SDK .NET, Video Edit SDK .NET and Media Blocks SDK .NET run on all five major operating systems:

-   •Windows
-   •macOS
-   •Linux
-   •iOS
-   •Android

The classic engine of the first three SDKs runs on Windows only; their X engines and Media Blocks SDK are cross-platform. On Windows, these four .NET SDKs work with WinForms and WPF. Depending on the SDK, they also support WinUI, .NET MAUI, Avalonia, Uno Platform and the Unity game engine, and a separate Web Forms package adds an ASP.NET control for HLS playback in the browser. The SDKs target .NET Framework 4.6.1 and later (the Web Forms package needs 4.7.2) as well as modern .NET up to .NET 10. The DirectShow products, Video Edit SDK FFmpeg .NET and the Delphi and ActiveX components are Windows-only.

## Who Uses VisioForge

Developers use our SDKs to build video surveillance and NVR software, call-center recording, broadcasting and live-streaming tools, video editors and media players, and applications for research, museums and education.

Organizations that have used VisioForge SDKs include Bosch, BBC, Siemens, Autodesk, Alcatel-Lucent, McLaren, Interplay Sports, Duke University Medical Center, Los Alamos National Laboratory, the City of Colorado Springs, The Tech Museum of Innovation and the Ontario Science Centre.

Paid licenses are royalty-free, and each SDK ships with demo applications and online documentation. Support is available by email, through our helpdesk and on Discord.

## Licensing in brief

### Developer license

One named developer. 12 months of minor and major updates and email support. As a subscription it renews yearly and can be cancelled at any time; a one-time payment covers 12 months. The last version you downloaded stays yours.

### Workgroup license

Three named developers in one organization. Otherwise identical to the Developer license: 12 months of updates and email support.

### Lifetime·Team license

Every developer in your organization at one location in one city. Perpetual use, lifetime minor and major updates and email support.

### After purchase

Payment is handled by Stripe. The .vflicense files arrive by email within minutes of the payment being confirmed; if they do not, write to [support@visioforge.com](mailto:support@visioforge.com). An application you have already built keeps working after the license expires; only newer SDK releases need a new license.

### Payment and extras

Subscription: card or SEPA Direct Debit. One-time payment: also iDEAL, Klarna, Alipay, WeChat Pay and other methods, depending on the currency and your country. To pay by bank transfer, request an invoice. Prices are in euros. If the checkout opens in another currency, switch it to EUR to pay the listed price without the conversion fee. Custom filter and assembly names are available for orders of 10 or more licenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What's the difference between Developer and Lifetime·Team licenses?

A Developer license is a per-developer annual license assigned to one named developer and counted by developer, not by workstation. The annual license includes all minor and major updates and email support for 12 months from the purchase date. After expiry, the latest version released during the license period keeps working, and the license can be renewed at any time. The license can also be reassigned to another developer in the same company. A Lifetime·Team license is a single payment that covers all developers in the purchasing organization at one location in one city. The Lifetime·Team license includes minor and major updates and email support for the lifetime of the product, with no renewal. # C# Barcode Scanner for .NET from Live Video

Read QR codes and 1D barcodes in C# from a webcam, an IP camera, the screen or a video file. The barcode detector is a block in a .NET video pipeline, so you can scan the same video you preview, record or stream, on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.

[Download 30-Day Free Trial](https://files.visioforge.com/trials/visioforge_sdks_installer_dotnet_setup.exe)[View Pricing](/media-blocks-sdk-net#pricing)[NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks/)[Code Samples on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/.Net-SDK-s-samples)

From €500/year · Lifetime from €1,800

[Buy a license](/buy)

## A barcode scanner for video, not for scanned documents

Media Blocks SDK .NET and Video Capture SDK .NET read barcodes and QR codes from live video: webcams, IP cameras over RTSP or ONVIF, screen capture and video files. The detector runs inside the video pipeline and raises an event with the barcode type and value whenever it decodes a code in a frame. It is made for applications that already work with video, such as entrance and ticket checks, warehouse and production-line cameras or kiosks. If your input is still images, PDFs or scanned documents, a barcode library for images is the better fit.

## Barcode scanning in the two SDKs

|  | Media Blocks SDK .NET | Video Capture SDK .NET |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API | BarcodeDetectorBlock in a MediaBlocksPipeline; the OnBarcodeDetected event gives the barcode type, value and timestamp | VideoCaptureCoreX and VideoCaptureCore: set Barcode\_Reader\_Enabled and handle OnBarcodeDetected; VideoCaptureCore also takes Barcode\_Reader\_Type |
| Barcode types | QR Code, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, Codabar, ITF and GS1 DataBar (RSS-14), with UPC-A and UPC-E reported as EAN-13; Data Matrix with DataMatrixDecoderBlock | VideoCaptureCoreX: the same set as BarcodeDetectorBlock. VideoCaptureCore: QR Code, Data Matrix, PDF417, Aztec, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, Codabar, ITF and RSS-14 |
| Video sources | Any block with a video output: webcams and capture devices, IP cameras over RTSP and ONVIF, screen capture, video files and network streams | The capture sources of the engine: webcams and capture devices, IP cameras over RTSP and ONVIF, screen capture |
| Platforms | Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS | VideoCaptureCoreX: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. VideoCaptureCore: Windows |
| Edition | One edition with every block, the barcode detector included | The barcode reader is in every edition, Standard included; IP camera sources need Professional or Premium |

## How the scanner works

BarcodeDetectorBlock wraps the zbar barcode detector. It reads each video frame that passes through it and reports the codes it finds.

-   OnBarcodeDetected gives the barcode type, the decoded value and the timestamp of the frame on the pipeline timeline; UPC-A and UPC-E codes are reported as EAN-13
-   InputOutput mode passes the video on to a preview, an encoder or a stream; InputOnly mode only scans, for services without a screen
-   Scanning runs in the same pipeline as preview, recording and streaming, so one camera feed can be recorded and scanned at the same time
-   A code that stays in view is reported again on the following frames, so filter repeats by value in your handler
-   BarcodeDetectorBlock.IsAvailable() tells you before you build the pipeline whether the detector can run on this machine
-   Data Matrix codes are read by a separate block, DataMatrixDecoderBlock, built on libdmtx

## Where it is used

### Ticket and access control

Check QR codes on tickets and passes at an entrance with a webcam or a tablet camera, and show the live picture to the operator.

### Warehouse and production lines

Read barcodes on parcels and parts from fixed IP cameras over RTSP while the same stream is recorded for later review.

### Kiosks and self-service terminals

Scan a QR code shown on a phone screen in a WPF, WinUI 3, MAUI or Avalonia application.

### Recorded video and screens

Find the barcodes in a video file, or read QR codes shown on the desktop with screen capture.

## Frequently Asked Questions

How do I scan barcodes from a webcam in C#?▼

With Media Blocks SDK .NET, create a MediaBlocksPipeline, take the camera from DeviceEnumerator.Shared.VideoSourcesAsync(), and connect a SystemVideoSourceBlock to a BarcodeDetectorBlock in InputOutput mode and then to a VideoRendererBlock for the preview. Handle OnBarcodeDetected to get each code. With Video Capture SDK .NET, set Barcode\_Reader\_Enabled to true on VideoCaptureCoreX and handle the same event.

Can I read QR codes from an IP camera or an RTSP stream?▼

Yes. Create the source with RTSPSourceSettings.CreateAsync and RTSPSourceBlock, or with UniversalSourceBlock and the rtsp:// address, and connect its video output to BarcodeDetectorBlock. ONVIF cameras are read through their RTSP stream.

Can I use it in ASP.NET or a server-side service?▼

Yes. BarcodeDetectorBlock needs no window: in InputOnly mode it scans without rendering, so it runs in a console application, a Windows service or a background service of an ASP.NET Core application, on Windows or Linux. It reads the video that the server itself can open, such as IP camera streams, video files and capture devices attached to the server. It does not capture the camera of a visitor's browser.

Which barcode types does it read?▼

BarcodeDetectorBlock and VideoCaptureCoreX read QR Code, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, Codabar, ITF (Interleaved 2 of 5) and GS1 DataBar (RSS-14). Both report UPC-A and UPC-E as EAN-13: a UPC-A value arrives as 13 digits with a leading 0, and a UPC-E value arrives expanded to its 13-digit form. Data Matrix is read by DataMatrixDecoderBlock. The Windows engine VideoCaptureCore also reads Data Matrix, PDF417 and Aztec, and its Barcode\_Reader\_Type property selects one type or all of them; in the default Auto mode the event reports the type as Auto.

Does it work on Linux, macOS, Android and iOS?▼

Yes. BarcodeDetectorBlock and VideoCaptureCoreX run on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS; VideoCaptureCore is Windows-only. On Windows, macOS, Android and iOS the detector comes in the VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.\* NuGet packages. On Linux the SDK uses the system GStreamer, so call BarcodeDetectorBlock.IsAvailable() to check that the detector is installed. Android, iOS and macOS apps also need camera permission.

Do I get the same barcode more than once?▼

Yes. The detector reports a code in every frame where it decodes it, so a code held in front of the camera arrives many times. Keep the last value and time in your handler and skip repeats within a short window, as the barcode guide shows.

Which license do I need?▼

Media Blocks SDK .NET has one edition, and the barcode detector is part of it. In Video Capture SDK .NET the barcode reader is included in every edition, Standard included; IP camera sources need the Professional or Premium edition. One Video Capture SDK .NET license covers both engines, VideoCaptureCore and VideoCaptureCoreX. Prices are in euros, and VAT is added at checkout where it applies. The 30-day trial is fully functional.

# Broadcasting & Live Streaming SDK for .NET

Build professional live streaming and broadcasting applications with VisioForge SDKs. Stream to YouTube, Facebook, and custom RTMP servers. HLS adaptive streaming, SRT low-latency transport, NDI network video, DeckLink hardware output — all from C# and .NET.

## Broadcasting Development Challenges

### Multi-Platform Streaming

Delivering live video to YouTube, Facebook, custom RTMP servers, and HLS endpoints simultaneously requires managing multiple output protocols and encoding pipelines.

### Low-Latency Requirements

Professional broadcasting demands sub-second latency for live production, real-time monitoring, and audience interaction — standard HTTP streaming adds unacceptable delay.

### Encoding Complexity

Configuring H.264/H.265 encoders with proper GOP size, bitrate control, and keyframe intervals for each streaming platform while maintaining quality and performance.

### Hardware Integration

Integrating professional broadcast hardware like Blackmagic DeckLink cards and NDI sources/outputs requires specialized SDI/HDMI pipeline handling.

## How VisioForge SDKs Solve These Challenges

VisioForge Media Blocks SDK is a .NET SDK for building live streaming and broadcasting software in C#. It ships a dedicated sink block for each delivery target: YouTubeSinkBlock and FacebookLiveSinkBlock take a stream key, RTMPSinkBlock publishes to any RTMP server, HLSSinkBlock writes HLS segments and playlists and can serve them from a built-in HTTP server, and SRTMPEGTSSinkBlock and RISTMPEGTSSinkBlock send MPEG-TS over SRT and RIST. For studio hardware, NDISinkBlock publishes a named NDI source on the local network, and DecklinkVideoSinkBlock outputs SDI or HDMI through Blackmagic DeckLink cards in HD and 4K modes. Additionally, a TeeBlock splits one source into several branches, so a single application can preview, record and stream to several destinations at the same time. For example, a camera feed can go live on YouTube and to an SRT receiver while a local copy is recorded. Video Capture SDK .NET offers network streaming through a higher-level API.

-   YouTubeSinkBlock and FacebookLiveSinkBlock for one-line platform streaming
-   HLSSinkBlock with built-in HTTP server for adaptive streaming
-   SRT transport for low-latency, reliable streaming over lossy networks
-   NDI sink/source blocks for IP-based studio production workflows
-   DeckLink output blocks for professional SDI/HDMI broadcast hardware
-   Tee blocks enable simultaneous preview, recording, and streaming from a single source

## Key Broadcasting Features

### YouTube & Facebook Live

Stream directly to YouTube and Facebook Live using your streaming key. H.264 + AAC encoding with configurable quality settings.

### HLS Adaptive Streaming

Generate HLS playlists with configurable segment duration, playlist length, and built-in HTTP server. Ready for CDN distribution.

### SRT Low-Latency Streaming

Secure Reliable Transport (SRT) for low-latency streaming over unpredictable networks. MPEG-TS encapsulation with H.264/H.265 support.

### NDI Network Video

Send and receive video over IP networks using NDI protocol. Zero-configuration discovery for studio production environments.

### DeckLink Hardware Output

Output to Blackmagic DeckLink cards for professional SDI/HDMI broadcast. Support for fill-key, multi-output, and HD/4K modes.

### RTSP Server & Restreaming

Create RTSP servers to restream any source. Receive RTSP input, add overlays or processing, and re-publish to new endpoints.

## Pipeline Architecture

A VisioForge broadcasting pipeline is a chain of blocks connected in C#: a source, an optional TeeBlock that splits raw frames between a preview and the output branches, an encoder and one or more sinks. NDI and DeckLink sinks need no encoder. Sources include USB cameras, screen capture, RTSP IP cameras, NDI senders and DeckLink SDI inputs. Video is encoded to H.264 in software with OpenH264, to H.265 with SVT-HEVC on Linux, or to either on the GPU with NVIDIA NVENC, Intel Quick Sync and AMD AMF; audio is encoded to AAC. The SRT sink multiplexes these streams into MPEG-TS and supports caller, listener and rendezvous modes, a 125 ms default latency and AES passphrase encryption. The HLS sink writes MPEG-TS segments with a 5-second default target duration and can publish multivariant playlists, CMAF by default, for adaptive bitrate delivery. When the encoder's ParseStream setting is off, as for SRT, the SDK still keeps the parser for Apple VideoToolbox encoders and for H.264 on Android.

Source (Camera/Screen/RTSP)

Tee (Preview / Split)

Encode (H.264/AAC)

Stream

# A commercial GStreamer SDK for .NET and C#

Media Blocks SDK .NET is a commercial .NET SDK built on GStreamer. You build pipelines in C# from typed blocks — sources, encoders, effects and sinks — instead of string pipelines and raw elements, and you can still wrap any GStreamer element as a block when you need one.

[Download 30-Day Free Trial](https://files.visioforge.com/trials/visioforge_sdks_installer_dotnet_setup.exe)[View Pricing](/media-blocks-sdk-net#pricing)[NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks/)[Code Samples on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/.Net-SDK-s-samples)

From €500/year · Lifetime from €1,800

## Is there a commercial GStreamer SDK for .NET?

Yes. VisioForge Media Blocks SDK .NET runs its media pipelines on GStreamer and is sold with a commercial license and VisioForge support. It is not a one-to-one copy of the GStreamer API: each block wraps one or more GStreamer elements behind a C# class with a settings object, and MediaBlocksPipeline.Connect links the blocks. When the SDK has no block for an element you need, CustomMediaBlock wraps it by its factory name or a bin description, and hands you the raw Gst.Element.

## GStreamer bindings vs Media Blocks SDK .NET

|  | gstreamer-sharp bindings (GstSharp NuGet package) | Media Blocks SDK .NET |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What you program against | The GStreamer API itself, generated from GObject introspection: elements, pads, caps and bus messages | Typed blocks with settings classes, connected with MediaBlocksPipeline.Connect; raw elements through CustomMediaBlock |
| GStreamer runtime | Not in the package; you install or bundle GStreamer for every target platform | Windows, macOS, Android and iOS: native libraries in the VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.\* NuGet packages, plus a Java bindings project on Android. Linux: the distribution's GStreamer 1.22 or later (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 1.24) from its package manager, plus VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Linux.x64 or VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Linux.arm64 |
| Latest NuGet release | GstSharp 1.18.0, published in September 2020, with .NET Framework 4.5 assemblies | VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks, released with every SDK version |
| Elements without a wrapper | Every element is used raw | CustomMediaBlock wraps any element or bin description as a block |
| UI and platforms | Video output and UI integration are yours to build | Video views for WinForms, WPF, WinUI 3, MAUI, Uno Platform and Avalonia across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS; a Unity package for Windows, macOS, Android and iOS |
| License and support | Open-source bindings | Commercial license, royalty-free distribution, support from VisioForge |

## What Media Blocks SDK .NET adds on top of GStreamer

The SDK ships in the VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks NuGet package. GStreamer does the media work; the SDK gives it a C# shape.

-   Typed blocks instead of string pipelines: RTSPSourceBlock, H264EncoderBlock or MP4SinkBlock take a settings object, so a typo in an element or property name is a compile error rather than a runtime failure
-   Encoder selection: the parameterless H264EncoderBlock picks a hardware encoder when one is available and falls back to a software encoder
-   The runtime comes with the NuGet packages on Windows, macOS, Android and iOS; on Linux the SDK uses the distribution's GStreamer
-   Any GStreamer element when you need it: CustomMediaBlock takes a factory name or a bin description, sets properties from a dictionary and raises OnElementAdded with the raw Gst.Element
-   Your own typed blocks: subclass MediaBlock to wrap an element with a settings class and an IsAvailable() check, the same way the built-in blocks are written
-   The same engine in the higher-level SDKs: VideoCaptureCoreX in Video Capture SDK .NET and MediaPlayerCoreX in Media Player SDK .NET run on the same GStreamer-based pipeline

## Frequently Asked Questions

Does a commercial .NET SDK for GStreamer exist?▼

Yes. Media Blocks SDK .NET from VisioForge is a commercial .NET SDK built on GStreamer. It is installed from the VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks NuGet package, licensed commercially with royalty-free distribution, and supported by VisioForge.

Is Media Blocks SDK .NET a one-to-one wrapper of the GStreamer API?▼

No. It is a pipeline SDK on top of GStreamer: you work with typed blocks such as RTSPSourceBlock, H264EncoderBlock and MP4SinkBlock and connect them with MediaBlocksPipeline.Connect. Elements, pads and caps are handled inside the blocks. When you need the element itself, CustomMediaBlock and the OnElementAdded event give you the raw Gst.Element.

Can I use a GStreamer element the SDK does not wrap?▼

Yes. Create CustomMediaBlockSettings with the element's factory name, declare its input and output pads, put property values into ElementParams and pass the settings to CustomMediaBlock. Elements that create their pads at runtime, such as demuxers, are supported with UsePadAddedEvent. For reuse, subclass MediaBlock to make a typed block of your own.

Can I use a gst-launch pipeline description?▼

Within a block, yes. CustomMediaBlock accepts a bin description in square brackets, for example "\[ videoconvert ! videobalance saturation=0 ! videoconvert \]", and parses it into one bin with input and output pads. The pipeline around it, from source to sink, is built from blocks.

Do I need to install GStreamer separately?▼

On Windows, macOS, Android and iOS, no: the GStreamer libraries come in the VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.\* NuGet packages for each platform. On Android, the app also adds a project reference to the Java bindings project VisioForge.Core.Android.X10.csproj from the VisioForge samples repository. On Linux, the SDK uses the distribution's GStreamer, version 1.22 or later (Ubuntu 24.04 ships 1.24), installed with the distribution's package manager (apt on Ubuntu and Debian); add the VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Linux.x64 or VisioForge.CrossPlatform.Core.Linux.arm64 package.

Which platforms and UI frameworks are supported?▼

Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, with video views for WinForms, WPF, WinUI 3, .NET MAUI, Uno Platform and Avalonia. The Unity package targets Windows, macOS, Android and iOS.

How do I try it?▼

Download the fully functional 30-day trial or add the VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks package from NuGet and run the samples. Depending on the output, a watermark or unregistered notice may appear until a license is applied. Licenses are sold per year or as a lifetime license; prices are on the Media Blocks SDK .NET page.

## KLV / MISB Metadata SDK for .NET: KLV in MPEG-TS
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/solutions/klv-misb-metadata

# KLV / MISB Metadata SDK for .NET

Read KLV telemetry out of MPEG-TS, decode MISB ST 0601 elements, and record or restream live MISB feeds with the metadata kept — from C# and .NET.

[Download 30-Day Free Trial](https://files.visioforge.com/trials/visioforge_sdks_installer_dotnet_setup.exe)[View Pricing](/media-blocks-sdk-net#pricing)[NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks/)[Code Samples on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/.Net-SDK-s-samples)

From €500/year · Lifetime from €1,800

## What KLV and MISB are

KLV (Key-Length-Value, SMPTE ST 336) is the binary encoding that UAV, ISR and surveillance systems use to carry telemetry beside the video: time stamps, platform and sensor position, orientation, and the geolocation of the frame center. MISB ST 0601 (the UAS Datalink Local Set) defines those fields, and MISB / STANAG 4609 streams carry them as a separate metadata stream inside MPEG-TS.

## What the SDK does with KLV

Two VisioForge SDKs handle KLV: Media Blocks SDK works with KLV in MPEG-TS files on Windows, Linux and macOS, and Video Capture SDK passes live KLV from an IP camera or UDP source into a recording or a restream on Windows.

-   Extract: MPEGTSDemuxBlock exposes the metadata stream of an MPEG-TS file on its MetadataOutput pad, and KLVFileSinkBlock writes the KLV packets to a .klv file
-   Decode: KLVParser reads MISB ST 0601 local-set elements — more than 90 of them, from precision time stamp to sensor and frame-center coordinates — and handles the BER-encoded lengths MISB uses
-   Embed (Media Blocks): MPEGTSSinkSettings.Metadata takes a KLVMetadata object built from a .klv file or a byte array; it is muxed as one static payload, not a per-frame timed track
-   Record and restream live KLV (Video Capture SDK, Windows): MPEGTSOutput.KLVEnabled muxes KLV from the source into the MPEG-TS file, and FFMPEGEXEOutput.KLVEnabled carries it in MPEG-TS, RTP MPEG-TS and HLS output (for file recording, also set UsePipe)
-   Read live packets: the OnDataFrameBuffer event delivers each KLV packet with its size and timestamp (DataFrameType.KLV)

## License Plate Recognition (ANPR/LPR) in C# and .NET
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/solutions/license-plate-recognition-dotnet

# License plate recognition (ANPR/LPR) in C# and .NET

Read vehicle license plates from IP cameras, webcams and video files in C#. LicensePlateRecognizerBlock finds each plate, reads it and reports the text with a timestamp — on the device, in the same pipeline that previews, records and streams the video.

[Download 30-Day Free Trial](https://files.visioforge.com/trials/visioforge_sdks_installer_dotnet_setup.exe)[View Pricing](/media-blocks-sdk-net#pricing)[NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks/)[Code Samples on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/.Net-SDK-s-samples)

From €500/year · Lifetime from €1,800

## A plate reader is not general OCR pointed at a car

Automatic number plate recognition — ANPR, also called ALPR, LPR or licence plate recognition — is not general OCR. General OCR reads every sign, sticker and logo in the frame and does not know which text is the plate. ANPR needs two models: a detector that finds plates and an OCR model trained on plate characters. You also need the frames — decoded from the camera, picked at a rate the hardware can keep up with, without stalling the live video. In VisioForge SDKs, LicensePlateRecognizerBlock is a block of the video pipeline: the SDK decodes the source, the block runs both models on a background thread, and the frames continue to the screen, a file or a network stream.

## Building ANPR yourself or calling a cloud API vs. LicensePlateRecognizerBlock

|  | Typical do-it-yourself or cloud ANPR | LicensePlateRecognizerBlock in a VisioForge pipeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Finding the plate | Find or train a plate detector, export it to ONNX, write the pre- and post-processing | FastALPR YOLOv9-T plate detector (MIT); DetectionConfidenceThreshold and MaxDetections |
| Reading the characters | General OCR that also reads every other text in the frame | A plate-specific fast-plate-ocr head; Text comes uppercased, with non-alphanumeric characters removed |
| Getting frames from the camera | A separate decoder or frame grabber for each kind of source | Any SDK source: RTSP IP cameras, webcams, video files |
| Keeping live video smooth | Recognition on the capture thread stalls the stream | Recognition runs on a background worker; frames that arrive while it is busy are skipped and counted |
| Plates from different countries | Retrain the model or change provider | A global head for the USA and 90+ countries and a European head for EU plates, chosen with RecognitionModelPath |
| Where the video goes | Frames sent to a cloud service and billed per call | Nowhere: ONNX Runtime in your process, no API key, no per-call fee |

## What the ANPR block gives you

LicensePlateRecognizerBlock ships in the VisioForge.DotNet.Core.AI package. It has one video input and one video output, runs two ONNX models on the frames it receives and reports plates through the OnPlateRecognized event.

-   Two-stage recognition: a YOLOv9-T detector finds the plates, and each cropped plate is read by a plate-specific OCR model; both are FastALPR models under the MIT license
-   A full result per plate: Text, Confidence (0 to 1), BoundingBox and the four-point Polygon in source-frame pixels, with the frame Timestamp on every event
-   Regional heads: the global head covers the USA and 90+ countries, the European head is tuned for EU plates; both read Latin characters (digits and A–Z), and the input size is read from the model itself
-   On the device: ONNX Runtime with DirectML on Windows GPUs, CoreML on Apple platforms and the CPU as fallback; ActiveProvider tells you which one is in use
-   Live video stays smooth: recognition runs on a background worker, FramesToSkip sets how often it runs, and LastInferenceTimeMs and DroppedFrameCount show how the hardware keeps up
-   Recognition next to recording: DrawResults draws the plate boxes and text into the frames that go on to the preview, a file or a stream
-   One block for every engine: connect it in a Media Blocks SDK .NET pipeline, or add it with Video\_Processing\_AddBlock to VideoCaptureCoreX or MediaPlayerCoreX

## Where it is used

### Parking access and payment

Recognize the plate at a gate camera to open the barrier or start a parking session.

### Toll and access-control logging

Record which plates passed a fixed camera and when, with the video kept on site.

### Fleet and yard management

Track vehicles entering and leaving a private lot or depot.

### Traffic review tooling

Flag plates for manual review; final enforcement decisions should always include a human check.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Does the video leave the machine?▼

No. LicensePlateRecognizerBlock runs both models with ONNX Runtime inside your process. There is no cloud service and no API key; frames and plate numbers stay on the device. The models are two .onnx files you ship with your application.

Which countries' plates can it read?▼

The FastALPR global recognition head covers the USA and 90+ countries; a separate European head is tuned for EU plates. Point RecognitionModelPath at the head for your region; the detector is the same for both.

Do I need to train my own model?▼

No. The block uses the FastALPR YOLOv9-T detector and the fast-plate-ocr recognition head as they are; you only supply the two .onnx files. They ship with the License Plate Recognition Demo.

What about busy scenes with many vehicles or distant plates?▼

The block reports up to MaxDetections plates per frame (10 by default). For small or distant plates, lower DetectionConfidenceThreshold or give the camera a closer view. On very busy scenes, a vehicle detector such as YOLOObjectDetectorBlock upstream can crop the vehicles first.

Which SDK do I need?▼

LicensePlateRecognizerBlock is in the VisioForge.DotNet.Core.AI package. Use it in a Media Blocks SDK .NET pipeline when you build the pipeline yourself, or add it with Video\_Processing\_AddBlock to VideoCaptureCoreX in Video Capture SDK .NET or to MediaPlayerCoreX in Media Player SDK .NET when your app already uses one of those engines.

Are license plates personal data?▼

Plates are commonly treated as personal data under privacy regulations such as the GDPR, and some jurisdictions have their own ANPR rules; review them for your use case before you deploy. To hide plates in a recording instead of reading them, PIIRedactionBlock blurs or pixelates them with the same plate detector.

## Cross-Platform Screen Recording in C# and .NET
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/solutions/screen-recording-csharp

# Cross-Platform Screen Recording in C# and .NET

Build a screen recorder in C# with one API for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS: the full screen, a window or a region, with sound, the cursor and click highlights, to MP4 or a live stream. Video Capture SDK .NET and Media Blocks SDK .NET use the native capture API of each platform.

[Download 30-Day Free Trial](https://files.visioforge.com/trials/visioforge_sdks_installer_dotnet_setup.exe)[View Pricing](/video-capture-sdk-net#pricing)[NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/VisioForge.DotNet.VideoCapture/)[Code Samples on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/.Net-SDK-s-samples)

From €250/year · Lifetime from €900

## A screenshot loop is not a screen recorder

Graphics.CopyFromScreen gives you one bitmap on Windows. A recorder also needs a steady frame rate, the cursor, sound, an encoder and a file whose audio stays in sync with the video, and on every other operating system the capture API is different again: AVFoundation or ScreenCaptureKit on macOS, X11 on Linux, MediaProjection on Android, ReplayKit on iOS. In the VisioForge SDKs the screen is a video source like a webcam. ScreenSourceBlock uses the native API of the platform it runs on, and the encoder, the file and the stream are the same code everywhere.

## Building a cross-platform screen recorder yourself vs. using the SDK

|  | Typical do-it-yourself stack | VisioForge Video Capture SDK .NET and Media Blocks SDK .NET |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capturing the screen | A different native API on each OS, each behind your own interop: Desktop Duplication or Windows Graphics Capture on Windows, ScreenCaptureKit or AVFoundation on macOS, X11 or PipeWire on Linux, MediaProjection on Android, ReplayKit on iOS | ScreenSourceBlock with one settings class per platform; ScreenSourceBlock() without arguments takes the platform default |
| One window or a region | Window identifiers and crop code that differ per OS: HWND on Windows, an X11 window ID on Linux | WindowHandle on Windows or XID on Linux for one window, Rectangle for a region, MonitorIndex on Windows or Monitor on macOS for the monitor |
| Cursor and clicks | Composite the cursor and click marks onto each frame yourself | CaptureCursor on Windows, macOS and Linux; MouseHighlight draws an expanding circle at each click, taken from a global mouse hook on Windows and passed in by your code on other platforms |
| Sound | A separate audio API per OS for the microphone, plus WASAPI loopback for system sound on Windows, synchronized with the video by your code | SystemAudioSourceBlock for a microphone on every platform, LoopbackAudioCaptureDeviceSourceSettings for system sound on Windows, on the same timeline as the video |
| Encoding and the file | Media Foundation, VideoToolbox and MediaCodec wrapped one by one, or an FFmpeg build shipped with each app | H264EncoderBlock picks MediaCodec, VideoToolbox, or NVENC, AMF and Quick Sync with OpenH264 as fallback; MP4, WebM, MKV, MOV, AVI or MPEG-TS output |
| Code to maintain | Five platform implementations to write, test and keep in step | One C# pipeline; only the source settings differ per platform |

## Screen capture on each platform

ScreenSourceBlock() with no arguments picks the default source for the platform. Pass a settings object to choose the API, the window or the region.

| Platform | Capture API | Settings class | Sound | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | Windows Graphics Capture, DXGI Desktop Duplication, DirectX 9, GDI | ScreenCaptureD3D11SourceSettings, ScreenCaptureDX9SourceSettings, ScreenCaptureGDISourceSettings | System sound (WASAPI loopback) or a microphone | Monitor, region or one window; click highlights |
| macOS | AVFoundation | ScreenCaptureMacOSSourceSettings | Microphone | Needs the Screen Recording permission: ScreenSourceBlock.AskPermissions() |
| Mac Catalyst (.NET MAUI) | ScreenCaptureKit | ScreenCaptureMacOSSourceSettings | Microphone | The same settings class as macOS |
| Linux | X11 | ScreenCaptureXDisplaySourceSettings | Microphone | Needs an X11 session; XID or XName selects one window |
| Android | MediaProjection | AndroidScreenCaptureSourceSettings | Microphone | The user accepts the system prompt; recording runs in a foreground service |
| iOS | ReplayKit | IOSScreenSourceSettings, IOSBroadcastSourceSettings | Microphone | Your own app, or the whole device through a Broadcast Upload Extension |

## What the SDK does for a screen recorder

Screen and desktop recording is a video source in VideoCaptureCoreX (Video Capture SDK .NET) and a ScreenSourceBlock in Media Blocks SDK .NET. Everything after the source works as it does for a camera: preview, recording, streaming and video effects.

-   Three capture modes: the full screen of any monitor, one application window by its handle, or a rectangle of the desktop
-   Windows Graphics Capture is selected by default on Windows 10 version 1803 and later; DXGI Desktop Duplication, DirectX 9 and GDI sources are also available
-   Sound from the PC through WASAPI loopback or from a microphone; in Media Blocks SDK .NET, AudioMixerBlock mixes both into one track
-   Cursor capture and click highlights with configurable color, radius and duration, for tutorials and demos. On Windows the clicks come from a global mouse hook: when MouseHighlight is set, VideoCaptureCoreX installs it on start; in Media Blocks you call MouseHighlightSubscribe(). On other platforms your code passes each click to MouseHighlightAddClickEvent (MouseHighlight\_AddClickEvent in VideoCaptureCoreX)
-   Hardware H.264: MediaCodec on Android, VideoToolbox on Apple platforms; on Windows the SDK tries NVENC, AMF and Quick Sync and falls back to OpenH264
-   Several outputs at once: record MP4 while streaming the same screen to YouTube over RTMP, SRT or NDI; pause and resume a recording or start a new file without stopping the preview
-   One API on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, from WinForms, WPF, .NET MAUI and native macOS, Android and iOS apps; a sample for each

## Frequently asked questions

How do I record the sound the PC is playing?▼

Use LoopbackAudioCaptureDeviceSourceSettings with an output device from DeviceEnumerator.Shared.AudioOutputsAsync(AudioOutputDeviceAPI.WASAPI2) and set Audio\_Record to true, as in the first example. For narration, use a microphone from AudioSourcesAsync instead. To record both, mix them with AudioMixerBlock in Media Blocks SDK .NET.

Can I record a window that is covered by other windows?▼

Yes, with Windows Graphics Capture: set API to D3D11ScreenCaptureAPI.WGC and WindowHandle to the window's handle. WGC captures the window's own content, so overlapping windows do not appear in the recording. A minimized window has nothing to draw and is not captured.

Does it work on macOS and Linux?▼

Yes. On macOS the screen source uses AVFoundation and needs the Screen Recording permission: ScreenSourceBlock.AskPermissions() shows the system prompt, and macOS applies a new permission after the app restarts. On Linux, ScreenCaptureXDisplaySourceSettings captures an X11 display, so the app needs an X11 session. The encoders, files and streams are the same as on Windows; system sound loopback is Windows only, so record a microphone there.

Can I record the screen on Android and iOS?▼

Yes, with Media Blocks SDK .NET. On Android, AndroidScreenCaptureSourceSettings takes the MediaProjection your app receives after the user accepts the system prompt. On iOS, IOSScreenSourceSettings records your own app through ReplayKit, and IOSBroadcastSourceSettings records the whole device through a Broadcast Upload Extension.

Why is the recording black?▼

Protected content such as DRM video is blocked from capture by the operating system. For other black frames, try the other capture API (WGC or DXGI Desktop Duplication) or the DirectX 9 source. On a laptop with two GPUs, Desktop Duplication has to run on the adapter that drives the display; DXGIAdapter selects it.

Which SDK do I need?▼

Video Capture SDK .NET if you want a ready capture engine: set Video\_Source, Audio\_Source and an output, then call StartAsync. Media Blocks SDK .NET if you build the pipeline from blocks, for example to add your own processing between the screen and the encoder. Both use the same screen sources.

## Surveillance Development Challenges

### Multi-Camera Management

Managing simultaneous connections to dozens of IP cameras with different protocols, resolutions, and codecs requires robust pipeline architecture.

### 24/7 Recording Reliability

Continuous recording demands efficient resource usage, automatic recovery from network interruptions, and reliable file output without corruption.

### Motion Detection Accuracy

Balancing detection sensitivity to minimize false alarms while catching real events requires configurable grid-based analysis with adjustable thresholds.

### Cross-Platform Deployment

Deploying surveillance solutions across Windows, Linux, macOS, and mobile platforms without rewriting the video pipeline for each target.

## How VisioForge SDKs Solve These Challenges

VisioForge Media Blocks SDK is a .NET pipeline SDK for building NVR, VMS and camera-monitoring software in C#. Each IP camera connects through an RTSPSourceBlock with a login and password, and ONVIF support covers camera discovery and PTZ control. Streams are recorded to MP4 for playback or to MPEG-TS, which stays readable if a recording stops abruptly. Additionally, every camera can run in its own pipeline, so a network drop on one camera does not stop the others. For example, a multi-camera NVR can show live views, record each camera and raise motion alerts from a single application. Video Capture SDK .NET offers the same camera support through a higher-level API.

-   Pipeline-based architecture handles multiple camera streams efficiently
-   Tee blocks enable simultaneous preview and recording from a single source
-   RAW capture mode records H.264/H.265 without re-encoding for minimal CPU usage
-   Built-in motion detection and face detection blocks with configurable sensitivity
-   Cross-platform .NET support: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS

## Key Surveillance Features

### RTSP/ONVIF IP Camera Support

## Video Editing Development Challenges

### Multi-Source Compositing

Combining cameras, screen captures, video files, and images into a single output with precise positioning, z-ordering, and alpha blending requires a robust mixer architecture.

### GPU-Accelerated Effects

Applying real-time video effects like blur, color grading, and custom shaders without dropping frames demands GPU pipeline integration with OpenGL/Direct3D.

### Format & Codec Diversity

Joining and rendering videos across MP4, WebM, AVI, MKV formats with different codecs, resolutions, and frame rates into a unified output.

### Audio Track Management

Replacing, mixing, or removing audio tracks from video files while maintaining A/V sync and supporting multiple audio formats (MP3, AAC, WAV).

## How VisioForge SDKs Solve These Challenges

Video Edit SDK .NET is a .NET SDK for building video editors in C#, and Media Blocks SDK adds pipeline-level compositing; the VideoEditCoreX engine and Media Blocks SDK run on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. VideoEditCoreX works at the timeline level: Input\_AddAudioVideoFile adds a clip with optional start and stop times for trimming, Input\_AddImageFile adds a still image for a set duration, and Output\_Format selects MP4, WebM, MKV, AVI, MOV, WMV or another container. Media Blocks SDK is built for custom compositing. VideoMixerBlock places each source in its own rectangle with a z-order and alpha, and fades it in or out at runtime. Additionally, VideoMixerStreamChromaKey removes a green, blue or custom background color, and LUTProcessorBlock applies .cube or .3dl color-grading files. For example, an application can key a presenter over a slide deck, grade the result and record it to MP4 while showing a live preview.

-   VideoMixerBlock composites multiple sources with positioning, z-order, and alpha blending
-   Chroma key (green screen) compositing with configurable sensitivity and noise levels
-   GPU-accelerated effects via OpenGL shader blocks (blur, color correction, custom GLSL)
-   LUT color grading with .cube/.3dl file support for cinematic looks
-   VideoEditCoreX joins video/audio/image files with format conversion
-   Audio replacement and mixing without re-encoding video tracks

## Pipeline Architecture

A Media Blocks SDK editing pipeline is a chain of blocks connected in C#: a source, optional mixer and effect blocks, an optional encoder and an output. Sources include video files through UniversalSourceBlock, cameras, screen capture and still images through ImageVideoSourceBlock. GPU effects run in an OpenGL section of the pipeline. GLUploadBlock moves frames to the GPU, GLShaderBlock runs a custom GLSL vertex and fragment shader, and GLDownloadBlock returns the frames to the CPU for encoding or display. Shader uniforms such as a blur radius can be changed while the video plays. The finished video is written by an output block such as MP4OutputBlock, which also holds the H.264 and AAC encoders. Additionally, a TeeBlock feeds the same frames to a preview window. For example, an audio track can be replaced without re-encoding the video when both codecs fit MP4: ParseBinBlock parses the original video stream, ParseBinBlock or MPEGAudioParseBlock for MP3 parses the new audio file, and MP4SinkBlock muxes both into a new MP4.

# On-device OCR for video streams in .NET

Recognize text in RTSP camera streams, webcams and video files from C#. OCR runs as a block of the Media Blocks SDK .NET pipeline — on the device, next to preview, recording and streaming.

[Download 30-Day Free Trial](https://files.visioforge.com/trials/visioforge_sdks_installer_dotnet_setup.exe)[View Pricing](/media-blocks-sdk-net#pricing)[NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/VisioForge.DotNet.MediaBlocks/)[Code Samples on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/.Net-SDK-s-samples)

From €500/year · Lifetime from €1,800

## Video OCR is not image OCR in a loop

An image OCR library takes one bitmap. To read text from a camera or a recording with it, you still decode the stream, pick frames, convert them, call the library and keep track of when each frame was shown. In VisioForge SDKs, OCR is a block of the video pipeline: the SDK decodes the source, OcrBlock reads the frames as they pass, and the same frames continue to the screen, a file or a network stream.

## Image OCR library vs OCR in the video pipeline

|  | Typical image OCR library | OcrBlock in a VisioForge pipeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | A bitmap your code passes in | Decoded frames from any SDK source: file, webcam, RTSP camera |
| Decoding the video | Your code, with a separate decoder or frame grabber | Done by the pipeline |
| Which frames are read | You pick and convert them | FramesToSkip; frames that arrive while OCR is busy are skipped and counted |
| When the text appeared | You track it yourself | Timestamp on every OnTextDetected event |
| Recording or streaming at the same time | A separate video pipeline | The same pipeline: OcrBlock output goes on to an encoder, a file or a stream |
| Boxes and text in the video | You draw them | DrawResults |

## What OCR inside the pipeline gives you

OcrBlock ships in the VisioForge.DotNet.Core.AI package. It has one video input and one video output and runs the PP-OCR models on the frames it receives.

-   Decoding is done for you: any source the SDK opens — video files, webcams, RTSP IP cameras — feeds OcrBlock directly
-   Text with time and place: each OnTextDetected event carries the frame Timestamp and, for every line, its Text, Confidence and BoundingBox
-   OCR next to recording and streaming: frames leave OcrBlock unchanged or with the text drawn in, and go on to an encoder, a file or a network output in the same pipeline
-   On the device: PP-OCR models on ONNX Runtime with the CPU, CUDA, DirectML or CoreML provider — no cloud API, no per-call fee, the video stays on the machine
-   100+ languages: point RecognitionModelPath and CharacterDictionaryPath at the PP-OCR model and dictionary for your language; the samples ship the Latin model
-   Cross-platform: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS from one C# codebase; the OCR sample also exists for .NET MAUI
-   Cost under control on live video: FramesToSkip = N runs OCR on one frame in N + 1; every setting and its default is in the OCR guide

## Where it is used

### Searchable recordings

Extract the text of recorded lectures, webinars and screen recordings with the timestamp of each line, and index it.

### Broadcast and signage monitoring

Check that lower thirds, tickers and digital signage show the expected text, on a live feed or a recording.

### Production lines

Read serial numbers, batch codes and printed labels from a fixed camera while the same stream is recorded for traceability.

### IP cameras in retail and warehouses

Read shelf tags and product labels from RTSP cameras on site, without sending video to a cloud OCR service.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Does the video leave the machine?▼

No. OcrBlock runs the PP-OCR models with ONNX Runtime inside your process. There is no cloud service and no API key; frames and recognized text stay on the device. The models are files you ship with your application.

How is this different from an image OCR library?▼

An image OCR library expects you to decode the video, choose frames and call it per bitmap. OcrBlock is part of the pipeline that decodes the source: it receives decoded frames, skips them according to FramesToSkip, reports each region with the frame timestamp, and passes the frames on to rendering, encoding or streaming.

Can I recognize text and record the stream at the same time?▼

Yes. Connect the OcrBlock output to an encoder and a file sink, as in the RTSP example above. DrawResults decides whether the boxes and text are burned into the recording.

Which SDK do I need?▼

OcrBlock is in the VisioForge.DotNet.Core.AI package. Use it in a Media Blocks SDK .NET pipeline when you build the pipeline yourself, or add it with Video\_Processing\_AddBlock to VideoCaptureCoreX in Video Capture SDK .NET or to MediaPlayerCoreX in Media Player SDK .NET when your app is already built on one of those engines.

Can I ship the OCR models in a commercial product?▼

The SDK runs third-party ONNX models and does not include model weights in the NuGet package. The PP-OCRv5 mobile models that ship with the samples are Apache-2.0. A model's license comes from its origin, so check the license of any other model, its weights and its training data before you ship it.

Can I combine OCR with other AI blocks?▼

Yes. LicensePlateRecognizerBlock, YOLOObjectDetectorBlock and PIIRedactionBlock have the same video input and output as OcrBlock, so they connect one after another in the same pipeline. To hide on-screen text instead of reading it, PIIRedactionBlock blurs or pixelates text regions found with the PaddleOCR models.

## Detect Pirated Video — Automated Piracy Detection SDK
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/detecting-pirated-video-content

# Detecting pirated video content

## Main information

Detecting pirated video content is essential for a new digital content era. Many types of websites offer users the ability to upload video content. Websites like YouTube exist solely for this reason, but many social networking sites also allow this capability. Such sites' immense popularity has attracted the ire of content producers who are getting serious about protecting their copyrights and putting real pressure on the owners of these types of sites to eliminate illegal infringement. A large amount of copyright-protected material – from clips from movies and TV shows to music and music videos – is readily available for download by visitors to these types of online video hosting services. While the site operators claim that they are operating under the Fair Use doctrine, content producers and large media companies aren't buying it. They have deep pockets and armies of lawyers at their disposal and are gearing up to take legal action. To avoid costly, protracted legal battles, online video upload sites pursue technologically-based methods of reducing and preventing copyright infringement on their sites.

## Detecting illegal content using Video Fingerprinting SDK

Preventing inadvertent liability for copyright infringement is a significant issue for any site that permits user-uploaded content. Copyright violations can result in costly and time-consuming legal action and could result in large civil or criminal liability. Our Video Fingerprinting SDK technology provides a perfect solution for these types of sites to continue providing video uploading and hosting of user content while minimizing the risks of copyright infringement. Video Fingerprinting SDK analyzes the content of a video, its colors, scene structure and the motion of objects, and turns it into a compact descriptor, the video fingerprint. A database of these video fingerprints can be created for copyrighted material. They can then be checked against video materials being uploaded by site users to detect the presence of copyrighted materials and disallow the posting of such materials to their websites.

## How automated piracy detection works

Video Fingerprinting SDK compares videos by their content, not by their files, so the check runs without anyone watching the uploads:

1.  Fingerprint each protected title once. A fingerprint takes about 1 KB per second of video and can be kept in a database; the .NET SDK includes a helper for MongoDB.
2.  Fingerprint each new upload, recorded broadcast or live stream as it arrives.
3.  Search the shorter video inside the longer one. The search returns the position of every match, so a clip cut from a film is found, and so is a whole film inside a longer upload. To catch an upload that mixes part of a film with other footage, fingerprint the film in short fragments (VFPFingerprintSource.StartTime and StopTime) and search each fragment inside the upload.
4.  Act on the result in your own code: block the upload, queue it for review or notify the rights holder.

## Quick facts

**Method**

Content-based video fingerprints: colors, scene structure, motion of objects

**Fingerprint size**

About 1 KB per second of video

**Speed**

About 300 ms to index one second of video; 1–2 ms to match two 10-second fingerprints (Intel i3)

**Survives**

New resolution, bitrate, codec or file format; a fragment inside another video

**Sources**

Video files, recorded broadcasts, live streams; HD and 4K

**Platforms**

.NET SDK on Windows, macOS and Linux; C++ SDK on Windows and Linux

**Deployment**

On-premise: runs inside your own application, no cloud service

**Samples**

Media Monitoring Tool, Media Monitoring Tool Live, Video Duplicates Finder, console samples

**Trial**

30 days, fully functional; may display a watermark or an unregistered notice

## What a match survives

A fingerprint describes what is in the picture: its colors, scene structure and the motion of objects. A copy is therefore still matched after a change of resolution, bitrate, codec or file format, and a fragment is found even when it is embedded inside another video. Fingerprints can be stored, copied and compared without the original files, so the reference library does not have to sit next to the uploads.

## C# example: match an upload against a protected film

This .NET example builds fingerprints as the vfp\_gen console sample does and searches as the Media Monitoring Tool sample does. It searches the shorter fingerprint inside the longer one, so it catches a clip cut from the film as well as the whole film inside a longer upload.

### C#

C#

Collapse

Copy

```csharp
using VisioForge.Core;
using VisioForge.Core.VideoFingerPrinting;

const int MaxDifference = 500; // MMT default; the MMT slider tunes it from 200 to 1000

await VisioForgeX.InitSDKAsync();
try
{
    VFPAnalyzer.SetLicenseKey("TRIAL");

    // Once per protected title: build the fingerprint and store it
    var filmFp = await VFPAnalyzer.GetSearchFingerprintForVideoFileAsync(
        new VFPFingerprintSource("protected-film.mp4"));
    if (filmFp == null) { Console.WriteLine("Cannot fingerprint the film"); return; }
    filmFp.Save("protected-film.vfp");

    // Load the stored fingerprint once, before processing uploads
    var film = VFPFingerPrint.Load("protected-film.vfp");

    // For each upload: fingerprint it, then search the shorter video inside the longer one
    var upload = await VFPAnalyzer.GetSearchFingerprintForVideoFileAsync(
        new VFPFingerprintSource("upload-1234.mp4"));
    if (upload == null) { Console.WriteLine("Cannot fingerprint the upload"); return; }

    var uploadIsShorter = upload.Duration <= film.Duration;
    var fragment = uploadIsShorter ? upload : film;
    var longer = uploadIsShorter ? film : upload;

    var positions = await VFPAnalyzer.SearchAsync(
        fragment, longer, fragment.Duration, MaxDifference, true);

    foreach (var position in positions)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(uploadIsShorter
            ? $"The upload matches the film at {position:g}"
            : $"The film appears in the upload at {position:g}");
    }
}
finally
{
    VisioForgeX.DestroySDK();
}
```

-   [Guide: search one video fragment in another](/help/docs/vfp/dotnet/samples/how-to-search-one-video-fragment-in-another/)
-   [MMT Live: detection in live streams](/help/docs/vfp/dotnet/samples/mmt-live/)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How can I detect pirated copies of my videos automatically?

Fingerprint your protected titles once and store the fingerprints. Then fingerprint every new upload or recording and search the shorter fingerprint inside the longer one with VFPAnalyzer.SearchAsync. A match returns its position, and your code decides what happens next, for example blocking the upload or sending it for review.

### Can it detect pirated content in live streams, including 4K?

Yes. Fingerprints can be built from a live stream as well as from files, and the Media Monitoring Tool Live sample searches a stream for reference fragments while it plays. HD and 4K video are supported.

### Does it still find a video that was re-encoded, resized or cut?

Yes. The fingerprint describes the content of the picture, so a copy is matched after a change of resolution, bitrate, codec or file format. A short clip taken from the film is found too, together with its position in the film. For an upload that mixes part of a film with other footage, search short fragments of the film inside the upload.

### Does the SDK search the web for pirated copies of my videos?

No. It compares the videos your application gives it: uploads to your platform, recordings, streams you capture. Crawling other websites for copies and sending takedown notices are not part of the SDK; they are work your own system does around it.

## DirectShow Filters — Source, Encoder and Video Effects
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/directshow-filters

# DirectShow filters for Windows apps

VisioForge makes six DirectShow products for Windows: two source filters, built on FFmpeg and on libVLC, that play files and network streams; a pack of encoder and muxer filters; a pack of video and audio processing filters; a virtual webcam and microphone; and filters that encrypt video. They work in any DirectShow application or filter graph, ship as x86 and x64 builds, and have C++, C# and Delphi APIs.

[Which filter do I need?](https://www.visioforge.com/directshow-filters#choose)[DirectShow bundle](https://www.visioforge.com/directshow-filters#bundle)

## What is a DirectShow filter?

A DirectShow filter is a COM component that does one step of media processing on Windows. An application connects filters into a filter graph: a source filter reads a file, a stream or a device, transform filters decode, process or encode the data, and a renderer or a file writer at the end shows or saves it. Filters ship as .ax files and are registered with Windows by an installer or regsvr32. A 32-bit application loads only x86 filters and a 64-bit application only x64 filters, so register the build that matches your app.

## Which filter do I need?

| I need to | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Play MP4, MKV, WebM, MPEG-TS and AVI files and RTSP, RTMP and HLS streams, with GPU decoding on NVIDIA, Intel and AMD | [FFmpeg Source DirectShow Filter](/ffmpeg-source-directshow-filter) |
| Play files and RTSP, HLS, SRT and HTTP streams through libVLC, including HEVC, VP9 and AV1 with DXVA2 or D3D11 decoding | [VLC Source DirectShow Filter](/vlc-source-directshow-filter) |
| Encode H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AAC, MP3 or Vorbis into MP4, MKV, MPEG-TS or WebM, with GPU H.264 and HEVC | [DirectShow Encoding Filters Pack](/encoding-filters-pack) |
| Add text and image overlays, color adjustment, deinterlacing, denoising, chroma key, motion detection, resize, crop or rotation, an audio equalizer or a volume booster | [DirectShow Processing Filters Pack](/processing-filters-pack) |
| Send video and audio from my app to Zoom, OBS Studio or a Chromium-based browser as a webcam and a microphone | [Virtual Camera SDK](/virtual-camera-sdk) |
| Record video to MP4 encrypted with AES-128 or AES-256 and play it back only with the key | [Video Encryption SDK](/video-encryption-sdk) |

## The six DirectShow products

Source filter

### FFmpeg Source DirectShow Filter

Decodes media with FFmpeg in any DirectShow app: MP4, MKV, WebM, MPEG-TS and AVI files, RTSP, RTMP and HLS streams, GPU decoding on NVIDIA, Intel and AMD cards.

[Product page](/ffmpeg-source-directshow-filter) [Documentation](/help/docs/directshow/ffmpeg-source-filters/)

Source filter

### VLC Source DirectShow Filter

Plays media through bundled libVLC: MKV, MP4 and MPEG-TS files, RTSP, HLS, SRT and HTTP streams, HEVC, VP9 and AV1 with DXVA2 or D3D11.

[Product page](/vlc-source-directshow-filter) [Documentation](/help/docs/directshow/vlc-source-filter/)

Encoder and muxer filters

### DirectShow Encoding Filters Pack

Encodes H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, AAC, MP3 and Vorbis into MP4, MKV, MPEG-TS and WebM, with GPU H.264 and HEVC on NVIDIA, Intel and AMD.

[Product page](/encoding-filters-pack) [Documentation](/help/docs/directshow/filters-enc/)

Transform filters

### DirectShow Processing Filters Pack

Text and image overlays, color adjustment, deinterlacing, denoising, chroma key, motion detection, resize, crop and rotation, plus an audio equalizer and volume booster.

[Product page](/processing-filters-pack) [Documentation](/help/docs/directshow/proc-filters/)

Virtual devices

### Virtual Camera SDK

Adds one virtual webcam and one virtual microphone to Windows. Zoom, OBS Studio, Chromium-based browsers and other DirectShow applications list them next to physical devices; apps that use only Media Foundation, such as the Windows Camera app, do not.

[Product page](/virtual-camera-sdk) [Documentation](/help/docs/directshow/virtual-camera-sdk/)

Encryption filters

### Video Encryption SDK

Encodes video to MP4 (H.264/AAC) and encrypts it with AES-128 or AES-256, keyed by a password or binary data. A matching decryptor filter plays the protected files.

[Product page](/video-encryption-sdk) [Documentation](/help/docs/directshow/video-encryption-sdk/)

## The filters work together in one graph

Each product is a set of ordinary DirectShow filters, so they connect to each other and to the filters Windows already has. For example, to convert a stream to MP4 with an overlay, the source filter decodes it, a processing filter draws the overlay, and the encoding pack compresses and writes the file.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between the FFmpeg and VLC source filters?▼

Both are DirectShow source filters that open files and network streams, and they use different engines. FFmpeg Source decodes with FFmpeg, with GPU decoding on NVIDIA, Intel and AMD cards. VLC Source plays through a bundled libVLC with DXVA2 or D3D11 decoding. Try both with your own files and streams during the trial.

Can I use the filters from C# and .NET?▼

Yes. The VisioForge.DirectShowAPI NuGet package provides .NET wrappers for the filter interfaces, and the samples cover C#, C++ and Delphi. Any language that can build a DirectShow filter graph can use the filters.

How do I register the filters on a user's machine?▼

Each product has an installer that registers its filters. To deploy with your own installer, register the .ax files with regsvr32 or from code, using the x86 build for 32-bit applications and the x64 build for 64-bit ones. The filter registration guide lists the file names.

Can I test the filters without writing code?▼

Yes. GraphEdit and GraphStudioNext list the registered filters, so you can build a graph by hand, connect the pins and play it before you write any code.

Which Windows versions are supported?▼

The filters run on Windows 10 and Windows 11; most products also support Windows 7, 8 and 8.1 and Windows Server. The exact list for each product is on its page. DirectShow itself is part of every desktop version of Windows.

Can I redistribute the filters with my application?▼

Yes. All six products are distributed royalty-free with your application under a purchased license. The terms for each product are on its page.

Is there a trial?▼

Yes. Every product page has a free trial download. The trial is fully functional; depending on the product and the output, it shows a watermark or an evaluation notice.

## GStreamer Metal Plugin — 15 GPU Video Effects on macOS/iOS
**URL:** https://www.visioforge.com/gstreamer-metal

Open Source · LGPL v2

# GStreamer Metal Plugin

GPU-accelerated video processing for GStreamer on Apple platforms. Seven Metal-based elements replace CPU-bound operations with zero-copy, single-pass GPU processing.

[View on GitHub](https://github.com/visioforge/gstreamer-metal)[Documentation](https://github.com/visioforge/gstreamer-metal/tree/main/docs)

## What is GStreamer Metal?

GStreamer Metal (gst-vf-metal) is a professional-grade GStreamer plugin that provides Metal-based implementations of common CPU-bound video elements for macOS and iOS. It delivers significant performance improvements through Apple's Metal framework with compute shaders, enabling real-time video processing with minimal CPU overhead.

### Zero-Copy Architecture

CVMetalTextureCache eliminates redundant CPU-GPU copies. Elements automatically skip GPU work when configured at identity/default values.

### Single-Pass GPU Processing

All filter effects (brightness, contrast, hue, chroma key, LUT, etc.) applied in one GPU dispatch — no intermediate frame buffers between effects.

### Mixed Format Compositing

Compositor accepts heterogeneous input formats (e.g., BGRA + NV12 simultaneously) with automatic format conversion.

### 6 Pixel Formats

Supports BGRA, RGBA, NV12, I420, UYVY, and YUY2 pixel formats across the element suite.

## GPU-Accelerated Elements

🎬

### vfmetalcompositor

Multi-input video mixing and compositing

-   Per-pad positioning, scaling, alpha, and z-order
-   Blend modes: source, over, add
-   Mixed format inputs (BGRA + NV12 simultaneously)
-   Sizing policies with aspect ratio preservation

🖥️

### vfmetalvideosink

Hardware-accelerated video renderer and display

-   GstVideoOverlay and GstNavigation support
-   Auto window creation with aspect ratio preservation
-   Mouse/keyboard event forwarding
-   BGRA, RGBA, NV12, and I420 formats

🎨

### vfmetalvideofilter

15 GPU-accelerated visual effects in a single element

-   Color: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, gamma
-   Effects: sharpness/blur, sepia, invert, noise, vignette
-   Chroma key (green screen) with tolerance controls
-   3D LUT color grading (.cube and .png formats)

🔄

### vfmetalconvertscale

Format conversion and scaling combined

-   All 6 format pairs supported (e.g., NV12→BGRA, UYVY→I420)
-   Bilinear and nearest-neighbor interpolation
-   Letterboxing with custom border colors
-   Replaces both videoconvert and videoscale

↻

### vfmetaltransform

Geometric transformations

-   8 rotation and flip methods
-   Per-edge cropping
-   Identity passthrough when no transform needed
-   BGRA, RGBA, NV12, and I420 formats

📺

### vfmetaldeinterlace

GPU-accelerated interlace removal

-   Bob, weave, linear, and greedy-H algorithms
-   Motion-adaptive deinterlacing (greedy-H)
-   Auto/manual field order detection
-   BGRA, RGBA, NV12, and I420 formats

🖼️

### vfmetaloverlay

Image compositing overlay

-   PNG and JPEG overlay support
-   Absolute and relative positioning
-   Custom sizing with alpha blending
-   BGRA, RGBA, NV12, and I420 formats

## 15 Video Effects

All effects are applied in a single GPU pass and can be animated via GstController:

Brightness adjustment (-1 to 1)

Contrast control (0 to 2)

Color saturation (0 to 2)

Hue rotation (-1 to 1)

Gamma correction (0.01 to 10)

Sharpness and blur (-1 to 1)

Sepia tone effect (0 to 1)

Color inversion

Noise/grain overlay (0 to 1)

Vignette darkening (0 to 1)

Chroma key (green screen removal)

Chroma key edge tolerance

Chroma key edge smoothness

3D LUT grading via .cube files (DaVinci Resolve/Adobe)

3D LUT grading via .png strip files

## Platform Support

### macOS

13.0+ (Ventura)

Dynamic library (gstvfmetal.dylib)

### iOS

14.0+

Static library (libgstvfmetal.a)

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is GStreamer Metal?

GStreamer Metal is an open-source GStreamer plugin that provides GPU-accelerated video processing elements for macOS and iOS. It uses Apple's Metal framework and compute shaders to replace CPU-bound video operations, delivering significantly better performance for tasks like compositing, color correction, format conversion, and deinterlacing.

### What platforms are supported?

GStreamer Metal supports macOS 13.0 (Ventura) and later and iOS 14.0 and later. On macOS it builds as a dynamic library (gstvfmetal.dylib), while on iOS it builds as a static library (libgstvfmetal.a) with a registration header.

### What pixel formats are supported?

The plugin supports six pixel formats: BGRA, RGBA, NV12, I420, UYVY, and YUY2. Most elements support BGRA, RGBA, NV12, and I420, while vfmetalconvertscale supports all six formats for maximum conversion flexibility.

### How do I install the plugin?

Clone the GitHub repository and run the included build script (./build.sh) for macOS. For iOS, use the CMake-based cross-compilation setup. The resulting library can be placed in your GStreamer plugin path for automatic discovery.

### Is it free to use? What is the license?

Yes, GStreamer Metal is completely free and open-source, released under the GNU Library General Public License v2 (LGPL v2). You can use it in both open-source and commercial applications without licensing fees.

### What GStreamer elements are included?

The plugin provides seven GPU-accelerated elements: vfmetalcompositor (video mixing), vfmetalvideosink (display), vfmetalvideofilter (15 visual effects), vfmetalconvertscale (format conversion and scaling), vfmetaltransform (rotation/flip/crop), vfmetaldeinterlace (interlace removal), and vfmetaloverlay (image compositing).

### Can I use it in iOS apps?

Yes. For iOS, the plugin builds as a static library (libgstvfmetal.a) with a gstvfmetal\_static.h header for static registration. It integrates with the GStreamer iOS SDK and supports the video formats commonly used on iOS.

### How does GPU processing compare to CPU-based elements?

GPU-accelerated processing provides significant performance improvements over CPU-based GStreamer elements. The zero-copy architecture and single-pass processing minimize data transfers and frame buffering. Elements automatically bypass GPU work when configured at identity values, ensuring no overhead when processing is not needed.

## Get Started with GStreamer Metal

Accelerate your video processing pipeline on Apple platforms with GPU-powered GStreamer elements.

# How to Register Your Purchased Product

Follow these steps to activate your license and unlock all features

## .NET SDKs (Video Capture SDK .NET, Media Player SDK .NET, Video Edit SDK .NET, Media Blocks SDK .NET)

VisioForge .NET SDKs use certificate-based licensing with .vflicense files. After purchase, you receive two files by email: a Developer certificate and a Release certificate.

### License File Types

#### Developer License

Use during development and debugging. The Developer certificate requires online activation.

#### Release License

Use in distributed applications. The Release certificate works offline and does not require activation on end-user systems.

### Embedded License Data

For .NET SDKs, load the .vflicense data from an embedded application resource. Do not deploy license files as external files beside your app; external files can be copied, replaced, or exposed, so this is not a secure registration model. Embedded license data is the correct registration model.

1.  1.Add the appropriate .vflicense file as an embedded resource: Developer for development and runtime tests, Release for distributed builds
2.  2.Construct each SDK engine or pipeline instance, load the embedded certificate into a byte array, and call SetLicenseCertificateAsync(byte\[\]) on that instance
3.  3.Call SetLicenseCertificateAsync(byte\[\]) before Open, Start, or Build. Protect the embedded resource against disclosure; contact support if you need a replacement certificate.

### C# — Embedded License Resource

C#

Collapse

Copy

Create the SDK instance, load the appropriate .vflicense bytes from an embedded resource, and call SetLicenseCertificateAsync(byte\[\]) before Open, Start, or Build.

```csharp
using System.IO;
using System.Reflection;

// Use the Developer certificate in development and the Release certificate in distributed builds.
#if DEBUG
const string licenseResourceName = "MyApp.Licenses.MediaBlocksSDK-Developer.vflicense";
#else
const string licenseResourceName = "MyApp.Licenses.MediaBlocksSDK-Release.vflicense";
#endif

// Load the certificate into a byte array from an embedded resource.
using var resourceStream = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly()
    .GetManifestResourceStream(licenseResourceName)
    ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("License resource not found");
using var ms = new MemoryStream();
await resourceStream.CopyToAsync(ms);

byte[] licenseData = ms.ToArray();

// Create each SDK instance first, then apply its certificate before Open, Start, or Build.
var pipeline = new MediaBlocksPipeline();
await pipeline.SetLicenseCertificateAsync(licenseData);

// Add and connect the required media blocks, then start the licensed pipeline.
```

## Troubleshooting

Invalid Certificate Error

Verify you are using the correct .vflicense file for your SDK product. Ensure the file has not been modified or corrupted.

Activation or Device Change

If a Developer certificate cannot be activated after a device change, contact support to deactivate the previous activation or resend the certificate.

Network Connection Error

Developer licenses require an internet connection for activation. Release licenses work offline. Check your firewall settings if activation fails.

SDK Version Not Covered

An Annual license covers SDK versions released during its 12-month update period. A Lifetime·Team license includes minor and major updates for the product lifetime.

Watermark or Unregistered Notice Still Appears

Create the SDK engine or pipeline, call SetLicenseCertificateAsync(byte\[\]) on that instance before Open, Start, or Build, and verify that the build contains the appropriate Developer or Release certificate.
